topic: E Se Você Salvasse Sua Escola de Uma Invasão Zumbi?
context: A 9-minute Brazilian 'What If' cartoon episode. A fungus spilled in the school science lab turns students into cartoon zombies: slow, arms stretched out in front, half-closed sleepy eyes, a soft lime-green glow around their bodies. Nobody bites, nobody gets hurt, and everyone is cured at the end. The zombies barely see, always follow the LOUDEST sound, and flee sunlight; 30 seconds of sun cures them. The hero, an ordinary kid, saves the school with knowledge: at noon he stands alone in the middle of the sunny school sports field and blows an orange referee whistle, leading hundreds of zombies out of the building into the sun. The tone is playful-tense, kid-friendly, never gory.

variants.scene: Sunny school sports field at noon, bright blue sky, empty grey stands behind. The gray-jacket mascot stands big in the right half of the frame, low angle, cheeks puffed, blowing a bright orange referee whistle held to his mouth, eyes determined. Behind him on the left, a huge crowd of round-black-head zombie kids in colourful hoodies and tees shuffles toward him with arms stretched straight out in front, sleepy half-closed white line eyes, each wrapped in a soft lime-green glow. Small white sound-wave arcs burst from the whistle. Text block bottom-left: APITA (white) over AGORA. (yellow, larger).

School cafeteria, long white tables, warm ceiling lights. The gray-jacket mascot crouches behind a green trash bin in the foreground right, big in frame, one black hand over his own mouth, wide shocked eyes with tiny pupils and a sweat drop, looking at the viewer. Just behind him, a line of round-black-head zombie kids in colourful clothes shuffles past with arms stretched out in front and sleepy half-closed eyes, each with a soft lime-green glow, one of them turning its head toward the bin. Text block bottom-left: ELES (white) over OUVEM. (yellow, larger).

Extreme close-up of the gray-jacket mascot's head and shoulders filling the right two-thirds of the frame under a blazing noon sun with strong warm rim light, smug half-lidded eyes and a sly smirk toward the viewer, an orange referee whistle hanging from a cord around his neck. Behind him, slightly blurred, a sea of round-black-head kids on a green sports field, the nearer ones still glowing lime-green with arms out like sleepwalkers, the ones in full sunlight blinking awake and confused. A big glowing yellow sun icon sits in the top-left sky. Text block bottom-left: 30 SEGUNDOS (white) over DE SOL. (yellow, larger).
